open_points.subject: refusal kinds
open_points.text: “the list of the kinds that failed in that stage”
open_points.question: When several failures in one stage have the same kind, does the refusal list that kind once or once per failure, and in what order are multiple kinds returned?
options: Return each distinct kind once in a declared order
Return one kind for every failed check, including duplicates, in check order
Treat kinds as an unordered set whose serialized order is unspecified
open_points.default_guess: Return each distinct kind once, in the refusal vocabulary's declared order.

witness.initial: An owner has a valid session and submits a new-project form whose display name and object address are both blank.
events: The owner submits the form with valid CSRF and request id.
witness.observer: The owner interface and any contract test inspecting the refusal see a different answer.

open_points.subject: owner_sessions.sign_out_owner admission boundary
open_points.text: Inputs require “The admitted session: the step of a sign-out request, which admit_owner_request runs holding the import lock and the session's lock”, but Errors declares “unauthenticated (no_owner_session) when no valid session is named.”
open_points.question: Does sign_out_owner receive only an already-admitted session, making no_owner_session impossible for this operation, or does it receive and validate an untrusted session identity itself?
options: Only admit_owner_request validates; sign_out_owner has no authentication error
sign_out_owner accepts a raw session identity and may return no_owner_session
Both validate, with the required precedence defined
open_points.default_guess: Only admit_owner_request validates; sign_out_owner receives an admitted session and has no authentication error.

witness.initial: The browser carries a cookie for a session that has already ended.
events: The owner submits a sign-out request.
outcomes: admit_owner_request returns no_owner_session and sign_out_owner is never called, as its Inputs require.
operations calls sign_out_owner, which returns its declared no_owner_session error.
witness.observer: The operations-to-owner_sessions module boundary and its contract tests see whether the public operation is called and which operation owns the refusal.

open_points.subject: duplicate project picks with differing values
open_points.text: “picks are a set, a project picked twice being picked once” while each pick carries “the display name and alias it arrives under”
open_points.question: If one project is supplied more than once with different display names, aliases, or associated Customer values, which values does the single resulting pick use, or is the request refused?
options: Coalesce duplicates only when all associated values are equal
open_points.default_guess: Coalesce only identical duplicates and refuse duplicates whose associated values differ.

witness.initial: A kept import file contains project P and the import is not closed.
events: The owner requests a mapping with P picked twice.
The first occurrence gives display name “Roof repair”; the second gives “Drainage repair”.
outcomes: The mapping shows P arriving as “Roof repair”.
The mapping shows P arriving as “Drainage repair”.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different mapping and would confirm a different imported display name.

open_points.subject: owner session cookie persistence
open_points.text: “Registry never expires or deletes the cookie”
open_points.question: Must the sign-in response create a browser-session cookie with no Expires/Max-Age attribute, or a persistent cookie, and if persistent what lifetime represents “never expires”?
options: Set no Expires or Max-Age; the browser may discard it when its browsing session ends
Set a persistent cookie with a specified finite lifetime
Set a persistent cookie with an effectively indefinite expiry
open_points.default_guess: Set no Expires or Max-Age and never send a deletion cookie; server-side session limits remain authoritative.

witness.initial: The owner signs in, and the server-side owner session remains within both its 8-hour and idle limits.
events: The browser receives the sign-in response and stores the cookie.
The owner closes and reopens the browser before the server-side session expires.
The owner opens the owner interface again.
outcomes: With a browser-session cookie, no cookie is sent and the owner sees the sign-in page.
With a persistent cookie, the cookie is sent and the existing owner session is accepted.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether reopening the browser preserves the signed-in session.
